hook: "I find it kinda crazy when I onboard brands that are doing 7 figs a month and they don't have email flows" — disbelief at a basic gap.
body: Math walk: 5 sales, 25–30% COGS — 4 from Meta at 20% margin, 1 recovered from an abandoned-cart email at 75% margin (no ad spend, "basically a free sale"); blended margin jumps to 31% from one email sale; flows raise CVR and margin at once.
idea: One recovered cart email out of five sales can lift blended margin from 20% to 31% — retention revenue is the highest-margin revenue there is.
sequencing: The disbelief hook (7-fig brands with no flows)
The math setup (5 sales, COGS 25–30%)
The Meta sales (4 at 20% margin)
The email sale (1 at 75% margin, free)
The payoff (blended 31%)
The principle (more sales from same traffic → CVR + margin up together)
formatting: Text post with photo; repeated/duplicated copy in the file (post appears twice).
why_it_works: The margin math makes flows feel like found money — "free sale" reframes retention from a nice-to-have into the single highest-ROI line in the P&L.
what_to_steal: Run LC's own version of this math: 30–50K monthly transactions with flows vs without — use it to justify flow investment internally.

hook: "You're not losing money because your ads suck. You're losing money because people who were ready to buy... leave." — reframes the problem from ads to leakage.
body: Teases an abandoned-cart sequence for 6-figure health brands that recovers sales "without spending another $1 on ads" (full thread linked, not in file).
idea: The leak, not the ads, is the money problem — ready-to-buy visitors who leave are the cheapest revenue to recover.
sequencing: Reframe: it's not the ads
The real loss: ready buyers leave
The scope: most 6-fig health brands never get them back
The tease: the sequence I'd use (thread)
formatting: Short text post with photo; thread-tease format.
why_it_works: "Ready to buy... leave" creates a vivid, painful image of money walking out the door — loss aversion aimed at the exact audience (health brands) most likely to feel it.
what_to_steal: The reframe for LC's cart-abandonment creative: "your stack is still in your cart" — target the leavers, not new buyers.

hook: "$15K revenue in the last 30 days. $1.7K MRR. not flexing. just sharing what I learned so you can skip my mistakes." — anti-flex numbers post.
body: Playbook rundown: sell the outcome not the software; multiple landing pages, let data pick the winner; real funnel with upsells/downsells/order bumps (1 visitor = 3x value); email sequences for every situation (abandoned cart, new user, old user — "money was just sitting there"); new creatives 3x/week; 10 versions of winners; +20% budget after 3 ROAS-positive days.
cta: "Save this. It took me a year to learn."
idea: Email sequences for every situation are "money just sitting there" — abandoned cart, new user, old user flows are the easiest revenue in the stack.
sequencing: Anti-flex numbers hook
Sell the outcome, not the product
Multiple LPs, data picks winner
Funnel: upsells/downsells/order bumps
Email sequences for every situation
Creative cadence (3x/week, 10 versions of winners)
Budget scaling rule (+20% after 3 ROAS days)
Save CTA
formatting: Text post with photo; checklist playbook, one lesson per line (826 likes, 1,735 bookmarks — highest engagement in the folder).
why_it_works: "Money was just sitting there" reframes flows as found revenue with zero marginal cost — the whole post is a checklist the reader can steal, which is why it got bookmarked 1,735 times.
what_to_steal: The "email sequences for every situation" checklist for LC: abandoned cart, browse abandon, new subscriber, post-purchase, winback — each is a line item of found money.

hook: "The 5 main things I check when a brand tells me they're stuck" — diagnostic checklist promise.
body: Five-point audit: (1) where traffic lands — cold to PDP is the ceiling, warm with advertorial/listicle/quiz; (2) creative diversity — 30 same-angle ads = 1 test, Meta groups lookalikes; (3) the offer — named bonuses, bundles, guarantees lift everything; (4) post-first-purchase — email flows (welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase second order); "a customer who breaks even on order one and buys twice more is wildly profitable"; (5) real research — Reddit, reviews, 1-star complaints in the customer's own words.
idea: Stuck brands almost never have an ads problem — they have a landing, offer, post-purchase flow, or research problem; fix leaks in order of cost.
sequencing: The 5-check frame
Check 1: landing (cold → PDP = ceiling)
Check 2: creative diversity (30 same angles = 1 test)
Check 3: the offer (bonuses, bundles, guarantee)
Check 4: post-purchase (flows = hidden money)
Check 5: research (customer's own words)
Closer: fix leaks one at a time, in cost order
formatting: Long text post; numbered diagnostic, consultant-audit style.
why_it_works: The "30 same-angle ads = 1 test" line and the Andromeda grouping insight make the audit feel current and expert — it diagnoses with specifics, not vibes.
what_to_steal: The post-purchase flow check for LC: welcome → abandoned cart → second-order push; and the "one change at a time" discipline for LC's own testing.

hook: "You can't retarget abandoned carts if Meta can't see the carts being abandoned." — obvious-but-missed truth.
body: Bottom-funnel retargeting (abandoned cart, checkout abandonment, DPA, product-view) only works if tracking is clean: pixel installed properly, catalog connected, events passed back (views, ATCs, checkout starts, purchases); a fresh pixel needs time + event volume before pools are meaningful; weak performance may be a tracking problem, not a strategy problem.
idea: Retargeting starts with tracking, not creative — if Meta can't see the events, the campaigns can't be built or trusted.
sequencing: The obvious truth (can't retarget what Meta can't see)
The campaigns that depend on it (cart, checkout, DPA, product-view)
The failure modes (bad pixel, disconnected catalog, broken events)
The principle: tracking before campaign complexity
The reframe: weak performance may be a data problem
The unglamorous truth (pixel events, catalog sync, attribution)
why_it_works: Gives underperforming advertisers a blameless diagnosis — "it's not your strategy, it's your data" — which is more actionable than another creative tip.
what_to_steal: The tracking-first audit for LC before any retargeting push: verify pixel events, catalog sync, and audience pool sizes before judging creative.

hook: "discovery ads are the closest thing to meta prospecting that exists inside google's ecosystem" — cross-platform arbitrage framing.
body: Deep dive on Google Discovery/Demand Gen ads: native-feeling ads in the Discover feed targeted on Google's intent graph (search, YouTube, browse history); the TOF play (warm traffic at scale into advertorials → remarketing pools); the Meta amplification loop (Discovery-educated viewers convert better on Meta retargeting 3–10 days later); creative rules (single lifestyle image showing the outcome, problem-first headline, curiosity description); targeting layers (in-market, custom intent, remarketing) with awareness-matched creative.
cta: "DM me if you want us to set up discovery campaigns for your brand" (agency pitch).
idea: Discovery ads are the bridge between Meta-style prospecting and Google-style intent — cold reach with warm conversion rates, feeding both Google remarketing and Meta retargeting pools.
sequencing: The positioning (Meta prospecting inside Google)
The surface (Discover feed = content environment)
The targeting edge (behavioral intent vs interest signals)
The native perception (brain classifies it as content)
The TOF economics (warm traffic → advertorial → remarketing)
The Meta amplification loop (educated viewers → better retargeting)
The creative rules (outcome image, problem headline, curiosity description)
The targeting layers (in-market, custom intent, remarketing)
The payoff claim (beats Meta prospecting 9/10 accounts)
DM CTA
formatting: Very long text post; mini-guide structure with subheads.
why_it_works: The "Meta amplification loop" is the novel insight — most brands silo platforms, but showing that Google touchpoints pre-educate Meta retargeting reframes cross-platform spend as one funnel.
what_to_steal: The cross-platform loop for LC: run Discovery/Demand Gen to jewelry-intent audiences → advertorial/quiz → Meta retargeting does the closing; and the creative rule (show the outcome — the stack worn — not the product).

hook: "If I took over a struggling store tomorrow... I wouldn't open the ads manager on day one: I'd start with the numbers." — contrarian operator take.
body: Six-step turnaround audit: (1) real P&L — some stores have a profitability problem, not a traffic problem; (2) cash position (reserves, inventory, supplier terms); (3) the offer — cheapest fix, lifts every ad (named bonuses, bundles, real guarantee); (4) where traffic lands — cold straight to PDP is the ceiling; (5) creative diversity — 30 same-angle ads = 1 test; (6) post-purchase flows. Fix leaks in cost order, one change at a time.
idea: Turnarounds start with the P&L and the offer, not the ads manager — the product is fine; the pricing, offer, page, or funnel is losing the sale.
sequencing: The contrarian frame (not the ads manager)
Step 1: real P&L
Step 2: cash position
Step 3: the offer
Step 4: landing
Step 5: creative diversity
Step 6: post-purchase flows
The principle: product last, fix leaks in cost order, one change at a time
formatting: Long text post; numbered turnaround playbook.
why_it_works: "The product comes last, and that surprises people" — the inversion of the expected audit order makes the whole framework memorable and quotable.
what_to_steal: The offer-first and flow-second checks for LC's Q4: named bonuses, bundles, guarantee strength, then welcome/cart/second-order flows before touching creative.

product: commentary — no product (an identity-resolution vendor pitch)
hook: "This 'multi-browser tax' is wasting 30-50% of your ad spend" — names an invisible cost.
body: The multi-browser identity problem: a shopper clicks an IG ad (in-app browser), enters email for 10% off; a week later buys in Safari; Klaviyo never connects the two, so the abandoned-cart email never sends and Meta/Google can't learn the conversion. Fixing identity typically boosts abandoned-cart revenue 40% and cuts CAC 10–15%.
cta: "Reach out if you'd like to see a demo" (Upstack pitch).
idea: Cross-browser identity breaks are silently killing cart-recovery flows — the same person looks like two people, so the reminder sequence never fires.
sequencing: The named cost ("multi-browser tax," 30–50% waste)
The scenario (IG in-app browser → email capture → Safari purchase)
The break (no identity link → no cart email, no platform learning)
The general rule (browser switches, cookie clears, 30+ day gaps)
The payoff (cart revenue +40%, CAC −10–15%)
The demo CTA
why_it_works: Naming the problem ("multi-browser tax") makes an invisible leak feel real and measurable — and the concrete scenario lets any brand owner check whether it applies to them.
what_to_steal: Audit LC's own identity continuity: does the cart email fire when a shopper moves from IG in-app browser to Safari? If not, this is found revenue.

hook: "The most underrated asset in your eCom business is probably sitting completely unused right now: Your email list." — asset reframe.
body: The one-pipe vulnerability: stores built on paid traffic collapse when CPA spikes or accounts get restricted; the email list is owned distribution; math walk (50 orders/day × $55 AOV × 90 days = 4,500 customers; one promo at 2% = $4,950 with no ad spend); the flow stack (welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase, winback, launches, flash sales, bundles); ads acquire, email infrastructure raises LTV.
idea: Ads acquire the customer; email infrastructure increases what that customer is worth — long-term winners own the ecosystem, not just the acquisition pipe.
sequencing: The underrated asset (email list)
The one-pipe vulnerability (paid-only stores)
The ownership contrast (Facebook owns reach; you own the list)
The math (4,500 customers → one send = $4,950)
The flow stack (welcome, cart, post-purchase, winback, launches)
The reframe (ads = engine, email = ecosystem)
The test (if ads shut off and revenue → zero, you lack infrastructure)
The closer (build the list, build the flows, let it compound)
formatting: Long text post; manifesto style with bullet flow stack.
why_it_works: The "if your ads shut off tomorrow" test is a gut-check every paid-dependent brand fails — it converts abstract list-building advice into an existential question.
what_to_steal: LC's version of the math: 300K SMS subscribers + email list → one send at 2% = the revenue line; and the flow stack as the Q4 checklist.

product: commentary — no product (an Omnisend partner pitch)
hook: "Let me guess — You built your abandoned cart flow when the store was doing 200 sessions a day. And nobody's touched it since." — painfully specific call-out.
body: The stale-flow problem: timing written for a smaller store, discount logic from different margins, send caps built for fraction of traffic; Q4's 10x volume through the same sequence produces more revenue, which hides that the flow never scaled; flows are the one system scaled without testing; now Omnisend runs inside Claude/ChatGPT (Connector Directory since July 30) so you can ask which automations are BFCM-ready, message by message.
cta: "Fix that before you build anything new for November. Check the next tweet for more info."
idea: Email flows are the one system that gets 10x'd without anyone checking whether it holds — audit message-level performance before BFCM, not after.
sequencing: The call-out (flow built at 200 sessions/day, untouched since)
The three staleness symptoms (timing, discount logic, send caps)
The hiding mechanism (more traffic → more revenue → looks fine)
The principle (wouldn't 10x ad spend without testing creative)
The new capability (Omnisend in Claude/ChatGPT, one question)
The message-level audit promise
The CTA (fix before November)
formatting: Text-only post; partner-pitch with a diagnostic frame.
why_it_works: "That growth is what hides everything" — the insight that rising revenue masks a decaying flow is the kind of counter-intuitive truth that earns the bookmark and the audit.
what_to_steal: LC's pre-Q4 flow audit: check every automation's timing, discount logic, and send caps against current volume — message by message, before November.
